subject: Post-call recap & next steps — competitive eval (model quality checks)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@datasync.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — competitive eval (model quality checks)

Thanks Alex — great chat earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Key requirements you reiterated:
- Low hallucination on factual Q/A and customer support prompts (target <= 2% on our sanity checks)
- Consistent instruction-following for multi-turn support flows
- Predictable regression behavior vs your current hyperscaler endpoint

2) What we (Redwood) will deliver this week:
- A side-by-side model-quality spreadsheet comparing Redwood + tuned open models vs your current hyperscaler endpoint (initial slice: support KB + API docs). See attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-eval-2026.xlsx
- Suggested eval prompt set (sample-eval-prompts.csv) and short-run regression checks (hallucination rate, answer correctness, instruction compliance)
- Proposed next test: run 2k prompt set across both stacks with identical decoding params and provide per-prompt diff + hallucination flags

3) Asks from you:
- Confirm the two personas we'd test: "Tier 1 support (technical)" and "Billing/Account support"
- Any IP/data constraints — do we run on your data only in Dedicated/private, or are synthetic redacted examples okay for the initial run?

4) Timeline
- We can run a first 200-prompt sanity pass within 24 hours after you confirm personas and give the green light to use the supplied sample prompts (attached). Full 2k sweep can be completed in ~48–72 hours after that.

If that all looks right, can you confirm personas and whether Procurement needs to be looped now? I'll schedule a short sync w/ Rishi to walk through the evaluation metrics.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-eval-2026.xlsx (workbook, 1 sheet)
Attachment: sample-eval-prompts.csv (CSV, 130 rows)

Thanks Marissa — that captures it well. Confirming the two personas (Tier 1 technical, Billing) — good to start there.

A few clarifications: 
- Hallucination threshold: Procurement is sensitive so we need documented methodology. Can you include a short note in the workbook about how hallucinations are flagged and examples?
- Data constraints: for initial run, anonymized/synthetic examples are fine. If results look promising we'll want to run on a subset of real transcripts (we'll coordinate on redaction).
- Procurement: looping them here so they see deliverables. They may have questions about retention and logs after the pilot.

Please proceed with the 200-prompt sanity pass. Thanks — looking forward to the spreadsheet.

Looping you both in to kick off the evaluation. Alex at DataSync confirmed personas and approved a 200-prompt sanity pass (anonymized).

Rishi — can your team run the following and drop results back into the workbook: 
- Sanity pass (200 prompts) across: Redwood-hosted tuned-Llama-3 variant, Redwood-optimized quantized variant, and DataSync's current hyperscaler endpoint (we only have them run their endpoint — they will provide output CSV).
- Metrics: hallucination flag (binary), hallucination severity (low/med/high), exact-match, token-level perplexity approximate, instruction-follow rate (manual sample 50 prompts), and a short note on localization differences where relevant.
- Regression checks: highlight prompts where hyperscaler is correct but Redwood variant is not, and vice versa.

Please use the sample-eval-prompts.csv attachment for this pass (I've included 200 rows labeled "sanity-200"). Default decoding settings: top-p 0.95, temp 0.2, max_tokens 512. If you think tuning is necessary for parity tests, note settings in the sheet.

Procurement will want a brief methodology doc line for hallucination definitions — add 2–3 example cases in the workbook.

Thanks — can we target an internal drop by tomorrow morning so I can send to Alex?

—
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — we ran the 200-prompt sanity pass overnight. High-level summary below; full workbook attached (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-eval-2026.xlsx).

High-level results (sanity-200):
- Overall hallucination rate:
  - Redwood tuned-Llama-3: 1.4% (3/200) — flagged as low severity (two short hallucinations, one medium where model invented a non-existent API field)
  - Redwood quantized variant: 1.9% (4/200) — low/med mix, slightly higher on long-context prompts
  - DataSync hyperscaler endpoint: 2.6% (5/200) — more likely to hallucinate on entity-heavy prompts
- Exact-match / correctness (human-labeled sample, 50 prompts):
  - Redwood tuned-Llama-3: 86%
  - Redwood quantized: 83%
  - Hyperscaler: 81%
- Instruction-follow rate (50-sample manual review): Redwood tuned 94%, quantized 92%, hyperscaler 89%
- Notable regressions: 6 prompts where hyperscaler was correct but Redwood missed; 9 prompts where Redwood was correct and hyperscaler missed. Details in worksheet "regressions".

Methodology notes added to workbook: hallucination flagged when a model asserts an undocumented API behavior, invents non-existent entities, or fabricates RPC endpoints. Examples included on sheet "methodology_examples" (3 cases).

Next recommended tests: 
1) Run 2k prompt sweep (same decoding params) and produce per-prompt diff + hallucination severity breakdown (we estimate ~48 hours compute).
2) Run an experiment with beam sampling vs nucleus to evaluate instruction-follow tradeoffs (we'll propose 3 decoding profiles).
3) If you want Dedicated/private testing on your redacted transcripts, we can schedule a secure run; procurement should confirm retention/logging controls.

I've uploaded the workbook and the sample logs to the Drive link Marissa included. Let me know if you want the raw CSV exports as well — we can share a compressed bundle.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
